headline: Dry and quiet, with chilly mornings and possible frost; only light rain possible late week.
summary: A large low pressure system aloft is staying well offshore and drifting south, keeping western Washington dry and quiet through midweek. The main thing people will notice is cold mornings. Monday lows should be in the 30s around Olympia and south along I-5, and in the 40s elsewhere. Tuesday morning is colder still, so frost is possible in the south Sound, the Chehalis Valley, the Cascades, and valleys. Patchy morning fog is possible in typical fog spots. Late in the week, a weak system may bring light rain Thursday into Friday. If it develops, snow could fall down to around 4,000 to 4,500 feet, bringing a few flurries to higher ground. Forecasters do not expect much impact, though the late-week picture is less certain.
changes: The morning discussion emphasized morning fog, possible freezing fog Wednesday, and a weakening front Thursday that would trim highs, while the afternoon and evening discussions shifted focus to frost and chilly mornings and described a weak system with only possible light rain late week.
